title: Path-conditioned training: a principled way to rescale ReLU neural networks
claim: Rescaling parameters before gradient descent changes optimization dynamics and speeds convergence, though the function and lifted-space geometry stay the same.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, shared color per initialization, dashed vs solid lines
description: Three side-by-side plots for a toy ReLU model, with each of three initializations drawn in its own color (blue, orange, green). The left panel is a log-log plot of loss against iteration. Dashed curves for vanilla GD sit on long plateaus, while solid PathCond curves drop sharply to about 1e-9 by around 1e4 iterations. The middle panel shows trajectories in the 2-D lifted space (uv, uw) over a grayscale loss-contour background with a colorbar. Dashed, solid and dotted paths run from marked init points toward the optimum, and the dotted path is GD on the lifted loss. The right panel is a 3-D parameter space (u, v, w) with dashed and solid trajectories, plus a gray curve of optimal parameters. A legend in each panel explains the line styles. The eye goes first to the left plot, where the solid curves fall away from the dashed ones.
caption: GD for a toy model $f_{\theta=(u,v,w)}(x) = u\relu(vx+w)$ on a loss $L(\theta)$ that can be factorized as $L(\theta) = \ell(\Phi(\theta))$ (see [ref]). (Left) Loss $L(\theta)$ during GD iterations for three different initializations $\theta_0$ (three colors). Dashed lines correspond to GD starting at $\theta_0$, bold lines to GD starting at rescaled $\theta_0^{(\lambda)} \sim \theta_0$ using \pathcond; (Middle) Trajectories in lifted space $\Phi(\theta) = (uv, uw)^\top$. Dotted lines are trajectories corresponding to $\partial_t \Phi = - \nabla_\Phi \ell(\Phi)$ (GD on $\ell(\Phi)$). (Right) Trajectories in parameter space.
abstract: Despite recent algorithmic advances, we still lack principled ways to leverage the well-documented rescaling symmetries in ReLU neural network parameters. While two properly rescaled weights implement the same function, the training dynamics can be dramatically different. To offer a fresh perspective on exploiting this phenomenon, we build on the recent path-lifting framework, which provides a compact factorization of ReLU networks. We introduce a geometrically motivated criterion to rescale neural network parameters which minimization leads to a conditioning strategy that aligns a kernel in the path-lifting space with a chosen reference. We derive an efficient algorithm to perform this alignment. In the context of random network initialization, we analyze how the architecture and the initialization scale jointly impact the output of the proposed method. Numerical experiments illustrate its potential to speed up training.
